newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper appoints new interior minister.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper appoints new interior minister.

text.p: Colombia's President Ernesto Samper appointed Carlos Holmes Trujillo as his new interior minister on Wednesday, the official government spokesman said.

Holmes Trujillo, 45, currently Colombia's ambassador to the Organisation of American States (OAS), will replace Horacio Serpa, who resigned on Tuesday to prepare his candidacy for the presidential elections in May 1998.

Holmes Trujillo, from southwest Valle del Cauca province, is a former education minister and served as a high commissioner for peace at the start of Samper's administration in a failed bid to kickstart negotiations with the country's leftist guerrillas.

One of the first challenges facing Holmes Trujillo will be to lobby lawmakers in the lower chamber of Congress to push through the government-sponsored bill to lift Colombia's 6-year-old ban on extradition. If the bill fails to win approval in two congressional debates by June 20 it may sink without trace for the remainder of Samper's administration.

In addition to announcing Holmes Trujillo's appointment, presidential spokesman Carlos Castillo said Colombia's vice president and ambassador to Great Britain, Carlos Lemos Simmonds, had been recalled to Bogota to head a National Council for Electoral Guarantees.
The council will oversee all aspects of campaigning in the lead-up to local elections in October and presidential elections next May.
